title: :not() and :has()
summary: :not(:last-child) adds separators between items; :has() styles a card based on what is inside it.
explanation: :not(X) matches everything X does not. .crumb:not(:last-child)::after puts a slash after every breadcrumb except the last, in one rule, with no extra rule to undo it. display: inline-block on the slash keeps the link's underline from running under it.
:has(X) is a parent selector: .card:has(.card-img) matches a card that contains an image, so only those cards switch to a two-column layout. Before :has() this needed a separate class added by hand.
:has() also works with states, as in .field:has(input:focus), which highlights the whole field group while its input is focused. Click into the input to see it.
tryThis: Remove :not(:last-child): the last crumb also gets a slash.
Delete the img from the first card in Items: it drops back to one column.
Change :has(input:focus) to :has(input:placeholder-shown) and type in the box.

children.text: This card has an image, so :has() gives it two columns.
